v8.title: Copilot Chronicle (CLI history and insights)
v8.description: Months of Copilot CLI history, read out of the CLI's own session store by chronicle_export.py and priced with GitHub's billed figure rather than an estimate. Chronicle history is the raw record; Insights per developer answers the questions a person asks about their own work. CLI only -- nothing done in VS Code chat reaches these streams. Every panel excludes service_user = 'schema_seed' and dedupes on chronicle_row_id; keep both when adding one.

panels.title: AI credits charged (chronicle)
panels.description: What GitHub actually charged for Copilot CLI, from chronicle's `total_nano_aiu`. This is the billed figure rather than a reading taken in flight, and it covers every CLI session ever recorded on this machine -- not only the ones since OpenTelemetry was switched on. Chronicle is a separate record from the live `lld_agent` feed and the two overlap, so these credits are never added to the credits on the other tabs. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(t.ai_credits), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.ai_credits
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t

panels.title: CLI sessions recorded
panels.description: Every Copilot CLI session in chronicle's store. This reaches further back than any other panel: session records start well before the first billed usage event, so an early session appears here with no credits beside it. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT s.chronicle_row_id
      FROM copilot_chronicle_sessions s
  WHERE s.service_user IN (${developer}) AND s.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t

panels.title: Credits per CLI session (chronicle)
panels.description: Billed credits divided by the number of sessions that actually spent any. Sessions with no usage event are left out of the divisor, so this is the cost of a session that did some work rather than an average dragged down by sessions that opened and closed. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.ai_credits) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.session_id), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.session_id, u.ai_credits
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t

panels.title: Prompt reuse % (chronicle)
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens served from cache instead of re-sent, as `cache_read_tokens` over `input_tokens`. Chronicle counts these the same way the spans do -- cache reads are part of the input total, never additional to it, which was checked: no row has more cache reads than input tokens. Long agent runs re-send the same context on every step, so a high figure here is the cache doing its job. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(t.cache_read_tokens, 0))
             / NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(t.input_tokens, 0)), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.input_tokens, u.cache_read_tokens
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t

panels.title: Billed credits over time, by what started the call
panels.description: Months of CLI spend, split by which actor made each model call. `user` is a prompt someone typed; `agent` and `sub-agent` are the model calling itself to carry the work out; `compaction` is the model summarising its own context so it can keep going. The shape of this chart is the point -- most of the money is spent after the human stops typing. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number. Bucketed with `date_trunc` and not with `histogram()`, which is what every other time chart here uses. On this stream `histogram()` fails outright with `[file_list] invalid time range` once the selected range passes a few weeks -- a plain aggregate over the same range and stream is fine, and `histogram()` over `lld_agent` at the same range is fine, so it is specific to asking for buckets across many months of backfilled partitions. A fixed daily bucket also keeps a bar comparable when the range changes, which for a history panel is worth more than an interval that adapts.

queries.query:
SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp)) AS "x_axis_1",
       ROUND(SUM(t.ai_credits), 4) AS "y_axis_1",
       COALESCE(t.initiator, 'unrecorded') AS "breakdown_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u._timestamp, u.ai_credits, u.initiator
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t
GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1
ORDER BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Who or what spent the credits
panels.description: The same split as the chart beside it, totalled. Read the `user` row first: it is the share of spend a person asked for directly, and everything else is the agent working on their behalf. A low `user` share is not waste -- it is what delegation looks like -- but it does mean the lever on cost is how tasks are scoped, not how prompts are worded. `unrecorded` is a call chronicle stored before it tracked an initiator. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT COALESCE(t.initiator, 'unrecorded') AS initiator,
       COUNT(*) AS model_calls,
       ROUND(SUM(t.ai_credits), 1) AS ai_credits,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.ai_credits) / NULLIF(SUM(SUM(t.ai_credits)) OVER (), 0), 1) AS percent_of_credits
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.initiator, u.ai_credits
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t
GROUP BY initiator
ORDER BY ai_credits DESC

panels.title: Model economics, billed
panels.description: Every model the CLI has used, ordered by what it cost. `Multiplier` is the rate GitHub applied to the request, which is why this table sorts on credits and not on calls: a model on a high multiplier can be a small share of the calls and a large share of the bill. `Credits / 1k output` is the same point per unit of work produced, and is the column to compare two models on. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT t.model AS model,
       COUNT(*) AS model_calls,
       MAX(t.request_multiplier) AS multiplier,
       SUM(COALESCE(t.output_tokens, 0)) AS output_tokens,
       ROUND(SUM(t.ai_credits), 1) AS ai_credits,
       ROUND(1000.0 * SUM(t.ai_credits) / NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(t.output_tokens, 0)), 0), 2) AS credits_per_1k_output,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.ai_credits) / NULLIF(SUM(SUM(t.ai_credits)) OVER (), 0), 1) AS percent_of_credits
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.model, u.request_multiplier,
             u.output_tokens, u.ai_credits
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY ai_credits DESC

panels.title: Credits by project
panels.description: Billed credits grouped by the working directory the session ran in. The directory is used rather than the repository because almost every session in the store has no repository recorded, so `cwd` is the only thing that says which project the work belonged to. Both sides of the join are deduplicated first: joined raw, a duplicated session row multiplies the credits of every call in that session, which measured exactly double the true total. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT s.cwd AS project,
       COUNT(DISTINCT u.session_id) AS sessions,
       COUNT(*) AS model_calls,
       ROUND(SUM(u.ai_credits), 1) AS ai_credits
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.session_id, u.ai_credits
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') u
JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT s.id, s.cwd
      FROM copilot_chronicle_sessions s
  WHERE s.service_user IN (${developer}) AND s.service_user <> 'schema_seed') s ON u.session_id = s.id
GROUP BY project
ORDER BY ai_credits DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.title: How fast each model answered
panels.description: Averages of what chronicle timed on every call. `First token` is the wait before anything appears, which is the delay a developer actually feels; `Between tokens` is how fast it reads once it has started. These are means over all calls, not percentiles, so one very slow call moves them -- read them for the difference between models rather than as a service level. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number. `duration_ms` is read through a CAST because a seed row once typed that column as text: `seed-schema.py` knew `duration_ms` as one of the columns Claude Code sends as a string and applied that to every stream with a column of the name, chronicle's included. The set is keyed by stream now, but a column's type cannot be narrowed again without deleting the stream, so the cast stays.

queries.query:
SELECT t.model AS model,
       COUNT(*) AS model_calls,
       ROUND(AVG(t.time_to_first_token_ms)) AS avg_first_token_ms,
       ROUND(AVG(t.inter_token_latency_ms), 1) AS avg_inter_token_ms,
       ROUND(AVG(CAST(t.duration_ms AS DOUBLE))) AS avg_duration_ms
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT u.chronicle_row_id, u.model, u.time_to_first_token_ms,
             u.inter_token_latency_ms, u.duration_ms
      FROM copilot_chronicle_usage u
  WHERE u.service_user IN (${developer}) AND u.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY model_calls DESC

panels.title: Files the CLI touched most
panels.description: The files Copilot opened or edited in the most separate sessions. A file near the top is one the agent keeps having to come back to, which usually says something about the file rather than about Copilot. No file contents and no edits are stored here -- only the path, the tool that touched it and when. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would inflate this number.

queries.query:
SELECT t.file_path AS file_path,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.session_id) AS sessions,
       MIN(t.first_seen_at) AS first_touched,
       MAX(t.first_seen_at) AS last_touched
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT f.chronicle_row_id, f.file_path, f.session_id, f.first_seen_at
      FROM copilot_chronicle_files f
  WHERE f.service_user IN (${developer}) AND f.service_user <> 'schema_seed') t
GROUP BY file_path
ORDER BY sessions DESC, file_path
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Credits the cache saved
panels.description: What prompt caching is worth, in credits: the cache read and cache write tokens re-priced at the plain input rate they would have been charged at with caching off, minus what was actually billed. Net, so the premium paid to write the cache is already subtracted from the discount earned by reading it. This is the number that says whether long sessions are paying for themselves. The credit figures come from `copilot_chronicle_costs`, which is chronicle's own price table -- `token_details_json`, one entry per token type with a cost per batch -- re-totalled per token type at backfill time. Recomputing the whole bill that way reproduces `total_nano_aiu` on every row in this store, so these are the billed credits split up, not an estimate of them. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(t.credits_cache_saved), 0), 0) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) t

panels.title: Credits spent writing cache
panels.description: Cache writes are charged at 2.5x the input rate, and they are the single largest slice of this bill after cache reads -- around a third of it. A write happens when the model sees context it has not cached yet, so a high figure means sessions are being restarted, or prompts keep changing the early part of the context. Compare it with the panel to the left: the writes are the price of the savings, and the two should be read together. The credit figures come from `copilot_chronicle_costs`, which is chronicle's own price table -- `token_details_json`, one entry per token type with a cost per batch -- re-totalled per token type at backfill time. Recomputing the whole bill that way reproduces `total_nano_aiu` on every row in this store, so these are the billed credits split up, not an estimate of them. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(t.credits_cache_write), 0), 0) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) t

panels.title: Credits spent on compaction
panels.description: What the model spent summarising its own context so it could keep going -- `initiator = 'compaction'`. Each one is expensive and none of it is work you asked for. A rising figure is the clearest signal in the dashboard that sessions are running past the point where starting a fresh one would be cheaper. The credit figures come from `copilot_chronicle_costs`, which is chronicle's own price table -- `token_details_json`, one entry per token type with a cost per batch -- re-totalled per token type at backfill time. Recomputing the whole bill that way reproduces `total_nano_aiu` on every row in this store, so these are the billed credits split up, not an estimate of them. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.initiator = 'compaction'
                          THEN t.credits_total ELSE 0 END), 0), 0) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) t

panels.title: Sub-agent share of credits (%)
panels.description: The share of spend made by sub-agents rather than by the main agent or by a typed prompt. High is not waste -- delegation is what the CLI is for -- but it does say where the lever is: a third of this bill was decided by how tasks were scoped, not by how prompts were worded. The credit figures come from `copilot_chronicle_costs`, which is chronicle's own price table -- `token_details_json`, one entry per token type with a cost per batch -- re-totalled per token type at backfill time. Recomputing the whole bill that way reproduces `total_nano_aiu` on every row in this store, so these are the billed credits split up, not an estimate of them. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.initiator = 'sub-agent'
                                 THEN t.credits_total ELSE 0 END), 0)
             / NULLIF(SUM(t.credits_total), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) t

panels.title: What to change, ranked
panels.description: Every finding below is a threshold over the numbers on this tab -- no model call, nothing scheduled, and the SQL is readable in the panel editor. A rule that is not over threshold returns no row, so an empty panel means there is nothing to act on. Severity is how much money is behind it, not how certain it is: `high` is worth changing this week, `review` is worth a look before it grows. Grouped by developer, so it says the same thing for one person as for fifty.

queries.query:
WITH costs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c.service_user, c.session_id, c.model, c.initiator,
         c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write
  FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
  WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')),
turn_rows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.chronicle_row_id, t.service_user, t.session_id, t.prompt_chars
  FROM copilot_chronicle_turns t
  WHERE t.service_user IN (${developer}) AND t.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')),
file_rows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT f.chronicle_row_id, f.service_user, f.session_id
  FROM copilot_chronicle_files f
  WHERE f.service_user IN (${developer}) AND f.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(f._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')),
session_rows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.chronicle_row_id, s.service_user, s.id, s.repository
  FROM copilot_chronicle_sessions s
  WHERE s.service_user IN (${developer}) AND s.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(s._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')),
per_session AS (
  SELECT c.service_user AS developer, c.session_id AS session_id, COUNT(*) AS calls,
         SUM(c.credits_total) AS credits,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(c.credits_cache_read, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cold_calls,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.initiator = 'compaction' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS compaction_calls,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.initiator = 'compaction' THEN c.credits_total ELSE 0 END) AS compaction_credits,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.initiator = 'sub-agent' THEN c.credits_total ELSE 0 END) AS subagent_credits,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.reasoning_effort = 'high' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_effort,
         SUM(c.credits_cache_write) AS cache_write
  FROM costs c GROUP BY 1, 2),
prompts_per_session AS (
  SELECT t.service_user AS developer, t.session_id AS session_id, COUNT(*) AS prompts
  FROM turn_rows t GROUP BY 1, 2),
prompt_totals AS (
  -- Counted per developer rather than summed out of per_session on purpose. Chronicle has recorded
  -- turns since May and billed calls only since July, so a session-by-session join silently drops
  -- every prompt from a session with no cost row -- which read as zero oversized prompts against
  -- the 25 the habits panel counts.
  SELECT t.service_user AS developer, COUNT(*) AS prompts,
         SUM(CASE WHEN t.prompt_chars > 20000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS huge_prompts
  FROM turn_rows t GROUP BY 1),
edited AS (
  SELECT f.service_user AS developer, f.session_id AS session_id, COUNT(*) AS files
  FROM file_rows f GROUP BY 1, 2),
model_calls AS (
  SELECT c.service_user AS developer, c.model AS model, COUNT(*) AS calls
  FROM costs c GROUP BY 1, 2),
top_count AS (
  SELECT m.developer AS developer, MAX(m.calls) AS calls FROM model_calls m GROUP BY 1),
top_model AS (
  -- Deliberately not ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...): this build rejects a partitioned window
  -- with "Expects PARTITION BY expression to be ordered". Max-then-rejoin needs no window at all,
  -- and MAX(model) settles a tie the same way on every refresh.
  SELECT t.developer AS developer, MAX(m.model) AS model, t.calls AS calls
  FROM top_count t JOIN model_calls m ON m.developer = t.developer AND m.calls = t.calls
  GROUP BY 1, 3),
agg AS (
  SELECT p.developer AS developer,
         SUM(p.calls) AS calls,
         SUM(p.credits) AS credits,
         COUNT(*) AS sessions,
         SUM(p.cold_calls) AS cold_calls,
         SUM(p.compaction_calls) AS compaction_calls,
         SUM(p.compaction_credits) AS compaction_credits,
         SUM(p.subagent_credits) AS subagent_credits,
         SUM(p.high_effort) AS high_effort,
         SUM(p.cache_write) AS cache_write,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(e.files, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS zero_edit_sessions,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(q.prompts, 0) > 20 THEN p.credits ELSE 0 END) AS long_credits,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(q.prompts, 0) > 20 THEN q.prompts ELSE 0 END) AS long_prompts,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(q.prompts, 0) BETWEEN 1 AND 5 THEN p.credits ELSE 0 END) AS short_credits,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(q.prompts, 0) BETWEEN 1 AND 5 THEN q.prompts ELSE 0 END) AS short_prompts
  FROM per_session p
  LEFT JOIN edited e ON e.developer = p.developer AND e.session_id = p.session_id
  LEFT JOIN prompts_per_session q ON q.developer = p.developer AND q.session_id = p.session_id
  GROUP BY 1),
outside_repo AS (
  SELECT s.service_user AS developer, COUNT(*) AS sessions,
         SUM(CASE WHEN s.repository IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_repo
  FROM session_rows s GROUP BY 1),
facts AS (
  SELECT a.*, COALESCE(o.no_repo, 0) AS no_repo, COALESCE(o.sessions, a.sessions) AS all_sessions,
         m.model AS top_model, m.calls AS top_model_calls,
         COALESCE(pt.prompts, 0) AS prompts, COALESCE(pt.huge_prompts, 0) AS huge_prompts
  FROM agg a
  LEFT JOIN outside_repo o ON o.developer = a.developer
  LEFT JOIN top_model m ON m.developer = a.developer
  LEFT JOIN prompt_totals pt ON pt.developer = a.developer)
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '1 high' AS "severity", 'Cache writes dominate the bill' AS "signal", ROUND(100.0 * f.cache_write / NULLIF(f.credits, 0), 0) || '% of credits (' || CAST(ROUND(f.cache_write, 0) AS BIGINT) || ')' AS "measured", 'A long thread rewrites its whole context every turn. Start a new session when the topic changes rather than growing one.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE 100.0 * f.cache_write / NULLIF(f.credits, 0) > 25
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '1 high' AS "severity", 'Long sessions cost more per prompt' AS "signal", ROUND(f.long_credits / NULLIF(f.long_prompts, 0), 1) || ' credits per prompt over 20 prompts, vs ' || ROUND(f.short_credits / NULLIF(f.short_prompts, 0), 1) || ' under 5' AS "measured", 'The same question costs more late in a session. Split the work before the thread gets long.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE f.long_prompts > 20 AND f.short_prompts > 5 AND (f.long_credits / NULLIF(f.long_prompts, 0)) > 1.5 * (f.short_credits / NULLIF(f.short_prompts, 0))
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '2 medium' AS "severity", 'Sessions that spent credits and edited nothing' AS "signal", f.zero_edit_sessions || ' of ' || f.sessions || ' sessions' AS "measured", 'Reading and explaining is worth paying for, but not at the top model. Use /model to drop before an exploration session.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE f.sessions >= 10 AND 100.0 * f.zero_edit_sessions / NULLIF(f.sessions, 0) > 40
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '2 medium' AS "severity", 'Calls that got no cache discount' AS "signal", f.cold_calls || ' of ' || f.calls || ' calls (' || ROUND(100.0 * f.cold_calls / NULLIF(f.calls, 0), 1) || '%)' AS "measured", 'Each of these paid full input price. Resuming a session keeps the discount; starting over from the same context pays for it twice.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE 100.0 * f.cold_calls / NULLIF(f.calls, 0) > 10
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '2 medium' AS "severity", 'Compaction is being paid for' AS "signal", CAST(ROUND(f.compaction_credits, 0) AS BIGINT) || ' credits across ' || f.compaction_calls || ' compactions' AS "measured", 'Compaction is the context overflowing. It is cheaper to finish a task and start fresh than to have the model summarise itself.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE f.compaction_credits > 0.02 * f.credits AND f.compaction_calls > 2
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '2 medium' AS "severity", 'Very large prompts' AS "signal", f.huge_prompts || ' prompts over 20,000 characters' AS "measured", 'A pasted log is charged as input and then again as cache. Point at the file and let the agent read the part it needs.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE f.huge_prompts > 5
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '2 medium' AS "severity", 'One model for everything' AS "signal", ROUND(100.0 * f.top_model_calls / NULLIF(f.calls, 0), 0) || '% of calls were ' || f.top_model AS "measured", 'Mechanical work does not need the strongest model. /model down for triage and log reading, up for design.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE f.calls > 100 AND 100.0 * f.top_model_calls / NULLIF(f.calls, 0) > 90
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '3 review' AS "severity", 'Sub-agents are a large share of spend' AS "signal", ROUND(100.0 * f.subagent_credits / NULLIF(f.credits, 0), 0) || '% of credits (' || CAST(ROUND(f.subagent_credits, 0) AS BIGINT) || ')' AS "measured", 'Not wrong -- delegation is often the cheap option -- but worth confirming the sub-agents are returning conclusions rather than re-reading the same files.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE 100.0 * f.subagent_credits / NULLIF(f.credits, 0) > 25
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '3 review' AS "severity", 'Work happening outside a repository' AS "signal", f.no_repo || ' of ' || f.all_sessions || ' sessions had no repository' AS "measured", 'Nothing is wrong with the spend, but it cannot be attributed to a project. Start the CLI inside the checkout when the work belongs to one.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE 100.0 * f.no_repo / NULLIF(f.all_sessions, 0) > 50
UNION ALL
SELECT f.developer AS "developer", '3 review' AS "severity", 'High reasoning effort' AS "signal", f.high_effort || ' of ' || f.calls || ' calls at high effort' AS "measured", 'High effort costs more per call. Check it is going to design and debugging rather than routine edits.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM facts f
WHERE 100.0 * f.high_effort / NULLIF(f.calls, 0) > 5
ORDER BY "severity", "developer"

panels.title: Where the credits go, day by day
panels.description: The same daily spend as the Chronicle tab shows, split by what the credits were actually bought: cache writes, cache reads, generated output, and fresh input. Read the proportions rather than the height. Output is the only slice that is unavoidable work; a day where cache write dominates is a day of restarts. Built as a UNION ALL over four columns of the same row, because the token type is four columns in the source rather than one dimension. Bucketed with `date_trunc` and not `histogram()`, which fails with `[file_list] invalid time range` on backfilled streams once the range passes a few weeks. The credit figures come from `copilot_chronicle_costs`, which is chronicle's own price table -- `token_details_json`, one entry per token type with a cost per batch -- re-totalled per token type at backfill time. Recomputing the whole bill that way reproduces `total_nano_aiu` on every row in this store, so these are the billed credits split up, not an estimate of them. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp)) AS "x_axis_1",
       ROUND(SUM(t.credits), 2) AS "y_axis_1",
       t.series AS "breakdown_1"
FROM (SELECT c._timestamp, 'cache write' AS series, c.credits_cache_write AS credits FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) c
      UNION ALL
      SELECT c._timestamp, 'cache read', c.credits_cache_read FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) c
      UNION ALL
      SELECT c._timestamp, 'output', c.credits_output FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) c
      UNION ALL
      SELECT c._timestamp, 'input', c.credits_input FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) c) t
GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1
ORDER BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Daily standup, by developer
panels.description: What `/chronicle standup` describes, counted instead of narrated -- and per developer, which the prose version cannot be. `Prompts` is turns, the number of times a person asked for something; `Model calls` is what that cost in requests, mostly the agent working on its own. The gap between the two columns is the story of the day. Days before 2026-07-09 show activity with no credits because chronicle recorded sessions for two months before it began recording usage events, which is why this is a FULL OUTER JOIN and not an inner one: an inner join would silently delete that history. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT COALESCE(a.day, s.day) AS day,
       COALESCE(a.developer, s.developer) AS developer,
       COALESCE(a.sessions, 0) AS sessions,
       COALESCE(a.prompts, 0) AS prompts,
       COALESCE(s.model_calls, 0) AS model_calls,
       COALESCE(f.files_created, 0) AS files_created,
       COALESCE(f.files_edited, 0) AS files_edited,
       ROUND(COALESCE(s.credits, 0), 1) AS ai_credits
FROM (SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp)) AS day,
             t.service_user AS developer,
             COUNT(DISTINCT t.session_id) AS sessions,
             COUNT(*) AS prompts
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t.chronicle_row_id, t._timestamp, t.service_user, t.session_id,
              t.turn_index, t.prompt_chars, t.reply_chars
       FROM copilot_chronicle_turns t
       WHERE t.service_user IN (${developer}) AND t.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) t GROUP BY 1, 2) a
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp)) AS day,
             c.service_user AS developer,
             COUNT(*) AS model_calls,
             SUM(c.credits_total) AS credits
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) c GROUP BY 1, 2) s ON a.day = s.day AND a.developer = s.developer
LEFT JOIN (SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp_micros(f._timestamp)) AS day,
             f.service_user AS developer,
             SUM(CASE WHEN f.tool_name = 'create' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS files_created,
             SUM(CASE WHEN f.tool_name = 'edit' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS files_edited
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT f.chronicle_row_id, f._timestamp, f.service_user, f.session_id,
              f.file_path, f.tool_name
       FROM copilot_chronicle_files f
       WHERE f.service_user IN (${developer}) AND f.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(f._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) f GROUP BY 1, 2) f
  ON COALESCE(a.day, s.day) = f.day AND COALESCE(a.developer, s.developer) = f.developer
ORDER BY day DESC
LIMIT 60

panels.title: Cost tips, computed: where each model's money went
panels.description: `/chronicle cost tips` as arithmetic. One row per model, and the three percentage columns always describe the same bill, so they read across: a model with half its credits going on cache writes is being handed fresh context repeatedly. `Credits per call` is what makes the premium models comparable -- opus costs an order of magnitude more per call than sonnet, and this is where to see whether the calls it was given were worth it. The GPT models show 0% writing cache because their cache writes are not charged. The credit figures come from `copilot_chronicle_costs`, which is chronicle's own price table -- `token_details_json`, one entry per token type with a cost per batch -- re-totalled per token type at backfill time. Recomputing the whole bill that way reproduces `total_nano_aiu` on every row in this store, so these are the billed credits split up, not an estimate of them. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT t.model AS model,
       COUNT(*) AS model_calls,
       ROUND(SUM(t.credits_total), 1) AS ai_credits,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.credits_cache_write) / NULLIF(SUM(t.credits_total), 0), 1) AS percent_writing_cache,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.credits_cache_read) / NULLIF(SUM(t.credits_total), 0), 1) AS percent_reading_cache,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.credits_output) / NULLIF(SUM(t.credits_total), 0), 1) AS percent_on_output,
       ROUND(SUM(t.credits_cache_saved), 0) AS credits_the_cache_saved,
       ROUND(SUM(t.credits_total) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 3) AS credits_per_call
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) t
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY ai_credits DESC

panels.title: Habits worth changing
panels.description: One row per developer, one column per habit the numbers can actually see -- the part of `/chronicle tips` that does not need a model to write it. A cold-cache call paid the full input rate because nothing was cached yet. An oversized prompt is usually a log file pasted in whole, and it is charged as input and then cached; the character count is the only thing read from the prompt, never the text. A session with no edit spent credits without changing a file, which is exploration -- fine in itself, worth knowing the volume of. Sessions outside a repository cannot be grouped by project by any panel here, which is why almost every project figure keys on the working directory instead. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT c.developer AS developer,
       c.cold_calls AS cold_cache_calls,
       ROUND(100.0 * c.cold_calls / NULLIF(c.model_calls, 0), 1) AS percent_cold,
       c.compactions AS compactions,
       c.high_effort AS high_effort_calls,
       COALESCE(t.big_prompts, 0) AS prompts_over_4k_chars,
       COALESCE(t.huge_prompts, 0) AS prompts_over_20k_chars,
       c.sessions_without_an_edit AS sessions_without_an_edit,
       COALESCE(s.sessions_no_repo, 0) AS sessions_outside_a_repo
FROM (SELECT p.developer AS developer,
             SUM(p.calls) AS model_calls,
             COUNT(*) AS sessions,
             SUM(p.cold_calls) AS cold_calls,
             SUM(p.compactions) AS compactions,
             SUM(p.high_effort) AS high_effort,
             SUM(CASE WHEN p.edited_files = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions_without_an_edit
      FROM (SELECT x.service_user AS developer, x.session_id AS session_id, COUNT(*) AS calls,
                   SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(x.credits_cache_read, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                     AS cold_calls,
                   SUM(CASE WHEN x.initiator = 'compaction' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS compactions,
                   SUM(CASE WHEN x.reasoning_effort = 'high' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_effort,
                   COALESCE(MAX(e.files), 0) AS edited_files
            FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) x
            LEFT JOIN (SELECT z.session_id AS session_id, COUNT(*) AS files
                       FROM (SELECT DISTINCT f.chronicle_row_id, f._timestamp, f.service_user, f.session_id,
              f.file_path, f.tool_name
       FROM copilot_chronicle_files f
       WHERE f.service_user IN (${developer}) AND f.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(f._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) z GROUP BY 1) e ON e.session_id = x.session_id
            GROUP BY 1, 2) p
      GROUP BY 1) c
LEFT JOIN (SELECT y.service_user AS developer,
             SUM(CASE WHEN y.prompt_chars > 4000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS big_prompts,
             SUM(CASE WHEN y.prompt_chars > 20000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS huge_prompts
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t.chronicle_row_id, t._timestamp, t.service_user, t.session_id,
              t.turn_index, t.prompt_chars, t.reply_chars
       FROM copilot_chronicle_turns t
       WHERE t.service_user IN (${developer}) AND t.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) y GROUP BY 1) t ON t.developer = c.developer
LEFT JOIN (SELECT w.service_user AS developer,
             SUM(CASE WHEN w.repository IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions_no_repo
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT s.chronicle_row_id, s._timestamp, s.service_user, s.id, s.cwd,
              s.repository
       FROM copilot_chronicle_sessions s
       WHERE s.service_user IN (${developer}) AND s.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(s._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) w GROUP BY 1) s ON s.developer = c.developer
ORDER BY developer

panels.title: Session shape: when starting fresh gets cheaper
panels.description: Sessions bucketed by how many prompts they carried, against what each prompt in them cost. The question this answers is the one every cost conversation ends on: does a long session get cheaper per prompt because the cache is warm, or more expensive because the context keeps growing? Read `Credits per prompt` down the column -- the answer is specific to how you work, and it is measured here rather than assumed. Sessions with no recorded prompts are absent by construction: the row count is driven by the turns stream. Aggregated over a DISTINCT-by-`chronicle_row_id` subquery, because a re-run of the backfill can leave the same source row in the stream twice and OpenObserve has no upsert; without it a duplicate would change this number.

queries.query:
SELECT CASE WHEN t.turns <= 2 THEN '1  1-2 prompts'
            WHEN t.turns <= 5 THEN '2  3-5 prompts'
            WHEN t.turns <= 10 THEN '3  6-10 prompts'
            WHEN t.turns <= 20 THEN '4  11-20 prompts'
            ELSE '5  over 20 prompts' END AS session_length,
       COUNT(*) AS sessions,
       ROUND(AVG(t.turns), 1) AS avg_prompts,
       ROUND(SUM(t.credits), 1) AS ai_credits,
       ROUND(SUM(t.credits) / NULLIF(SUM(t.turns), 0), 2) AS credits_per_prompt,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.cache_write) / NULLIF(SUM(t.credits), 0), 1) AS percent_writing_cache
FROM (SELECT a.session_id, a.turns,
             COALESCE(c.credits, 0) AS credits, COALESCE(c.cache_write, 0) AS cache_write
      FROM (SELECT y.session_id AS session_id, COUNT(*) AS turns FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t.chronicle_row_id, t._timestamp, t.service_user, t.session_id,
              t.turn_index, t.prompt_chars, t.reply_chars
       FROM copilot_chronicle_turns t
       WHERE t.service_user IN (${developer}) AND t.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(t._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) y GROUP BY 1) a
      LEFT JOIN (SELECT x.session_id AS session_id, SUM(x.credits_total) AS credits,
                        SUM(x.credits_cache_write) AS cache_write
                 FROM (SELECT DISTINCT c.chronicle_row_id, c._timestamp, c.service_user, c.session_id,
              c.model, c.initiator, c.reasoning_effort, c.credits_total,
              c.credits_input, c.credits_cache_read, c.credits_cache_write,
              c.credits_output, c.credits_cache_saved
       FROM copilot_chronicle_costs c
       WHERE c.service_user IN (${developer}) AND c.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  AND to_timestamp_micros(c._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')) x GROUP BY 1) c ON c.session_id = a.session_id) t
GROUP BY session_length
ORDER BY session_length

panels.title: Standup: what you have been working on
panels.description: The latest `/chronicle standup` -- Copilot reading the last day of your own history and reporting on it. It takes a period, so a capture of "standup last 7 days" appears here too, with the request shown next to the timestamp. Each capture is a billed model call, made by `scripts/chronicle-advice.py` over the CLI's ACP server; nothing here refreshes on its own. One finding per row, in the model's own words: after the report is captured it is handed back with an instruction to compress it to at most five one-line findings, and that is what this shows. A row captured before that existed falls back to shortening the report mechanically -- headline plus one sentence, cut at 200 characters -- and reads longer. The full report is in `copilot_chronicle_advice` either way. Compare it against **What to change, ranked** above: the numbers there are checkable, this is a narrative about them. The time picker does not move this panel: it always renders the single most recent capture in range, and the text describes whatever history /chronicle looked at when it ran rather than the selected window. So it can disagree with the numeric panels above, which do respect the window -- they are not the same claim measured two ways.

queries.query:
WITH lines AS (
  SELECT TRIM(u.line) AS raw
  FROM (SELECT unnest(string_to_array(r.source_text, chr(10))) AS line
        FROM (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(a.advice_summary, ''), a.advice_text) AS source_text,
                     ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY a._timestamp DESC) AS recency
              FROM copilot_chronicle_advice a
              WHERE a.service_user IN (${developer})
                AND a.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
                AND to_timestamp_micros(a._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')
                AND a.chronicle_command = 'standup') r
        WHERE r.recency = 1) u
), listless AS (
  SELECT regexp_replace(l.raw, '^([-*#>]+|[0-9]+\.)[ ]*', '') AS item
  FROM lines l
), split AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN regexp_like(s.item, '^\*\*.{4,150}?\*\*')
              THEN regexp_replace(s.item, '^\*\*(.{4,150}?)\*\*.*$', '$1')
              ELSE '' END AS head,
         CASE WHEN regexp_like(s.item, '^\*\*.{4,150}?\*\*')
              THEN regexp_replace(s.item, '^\*\*.{4,150}?\*\*[ :.\-\x{2013}\x{2014}]*', '')
              ELSE s.item END AS body
  FROM listless s
), clean AS (
  SELECT TRIM(regexp_replace(p.head, '\*|`|[.:]$', '', 'g')) AS head,
         TRIM(regexp_replace(p.body, '\*|`', '', 'g')) AS body
  FROM split p
), shortened AS (
  SELECT c.head,
         CASE WHEN regexp_like(c.body, '^.{30,170}?[.!?][ ]')
              THEN regexp_replace(c.body, '^(.{30,170}?[.!?])[ ].*$', '$1')
              ELSE c.body END AS body
  FROM clean c
), joined AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN s.head = '' THEN s.body
              WHEN s.body = '' THEN s.head
              ELSE s.head || ' — ' || s.body END AS line
  FROM shortened s
), kept AS (
  SELECT j.line
  FROM joined j
  WHERE LENGTH(j.line) >= 15
    -- A short line ending in a colon is a section label, not a finding.
    AND NOT (LENGTH(j.line) < 40 AND j.line LIKE '%:')
    -- The agent narrates before it reports, and that narration lands glued to the report header.
    -- Listed openers rather than a clever rule, so the next one is one string away.
    AND NOT regexp_like(j.line, '^(Analyzing |Good, enough data|Let me |I dug |Info: )')
), numbered AS (
  SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER () AS seq,
         CASE WHEN LENGTH(k.line) > 200 THEN SUBSTR(k.line, 1, 197) || '...' ELSE k.line END AS insight
  FROM kept k
), ranked AS (
  -- Number before deduplicating, not after: SELECT DISTINCT hashes the rows and the findings come
  -- back in hash order, which for advice is nonsense -- the report puts its most important one first.
  -- MIN(seq) keeps a repeated line where it first appeared; an empty standup says "Nothing to
  -- report." once per section and needs to say it once here.
  SELECT MIN(n.seq) AS seq, n.insight AS insight
  FROM numbered n
  GROUP BY n.insight
), meta AS (
  -- The capture time, on the panel rather than in its description. This is a stored
  -- document and not a query result: the newest capture in range, which the time picker
  -- does not change. Said where it is read, because a tooltip is not where anyone looks
  -- before trusting a number. No captures in range means no row, so the panel stays empty
  -- rather than announcing a NULL date.
  SELECT to_char(to_timestamp_micros(MAX(a._timestamp)), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS captured
  FROM copilot_chronicle_advice a
  WHERE a.service_user IN (${developer})
                AND a.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
                AND to_timestamp_micros(a._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')
                AND a.chronicle_command = 'standup'
)
SELECT h.insight AS "insight"
FROM (
  SELECT 0 AS seq,
         'Captured ' || m.captured || ' UTC - latest capture only, not filtered by the time picker' AS insight
  FROM meta m
  WHERE m.captured IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT r.seq, CAST(r.seq AS VARCHAR) || '. ' || r.insight
  FROM ranked r
) h
ORDER BY h.seq

panels.title: Tips: how to work with it better
panels.description: The latest `/chronicle tips` -- patterns Copilot noticed across your sessions, with the sessions named. This is about how you work rather than what it costs. Each capture is a billed model call, made by `scripts/chronicle-advice.py` over the CLI's ACP server; nothing here refreshes on its own. One finding per row, in the model's own words: after the report is captured it is handed back with an instruction to compress it to at most five one-line findings, and that is what this shows. A row captured before that existed falls back to shortening the report mechanically -- headline plus one sentence, cut at 200 characters -- and reads longer. The full report is in `copilot_chronicle_advice` either way. Compare it against **What to change, ranked** above: the numbers there are checkable, this is a narrative about them. The time picker does not move this panel: it always renders the single most recent capture in range, and the text describes whatever history /chronicle looked at when it ran rather than the selected window. So it can disagree with the numeric panels above, which do respect the window -- they are not the same claim measured two ways.

WITH lines AS (
  SELECT TRIM(u.line) AS raw
  FROM (SELECT unnest(string_to_array(r.source_text, chr(10))) AS line
        FROM (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(a.advice_summary, ''), a.advice_text) AS source_text,
                     ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY a._timestamp DESC) AS recency
              FROM copilot_chronicle_advice a
              WHERE a.service_user IN (${developer})
                AND a.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
                AND to_timestamp_micros(a._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')
                AND a.chronicle_command = 'tips') r
        WHERE r.recency = 1) u
), listless AS (
  SELECT regexp_replace(l.raw, '^([-*#>]+|[0-9]+\.)[ ]*', '') AS item
  FROM lines l
), split AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN regexp_like(s.item, '^\*\*.{4,150}?\*\*')
              THEN regexp_replace(s.item, '^\*\*(.{4,150}?)\*\*.*$', '$1')
              ELSE '' END AS head,
         CASE WHEN regexp_like(s.item, '^\*\*.{4,150}?\*\*')
              THEN regexp_replace(s.item, '^\*\*.{4,150}?\*\*[ :.\-\x{2013}\x{2014}]*', '')
              ELSE s.item END AS body
  FROM listless s
), clean AS (
  SELECT TRIM(regexp_replace(p.head, '\*|`|[.:]$', '', 'g')) AS head,
         TRIM(regexp_replace(p.body, '\*|`', '', 'g')) AS body
  FROM split p
), shortened AS (
  SELECT c.head,
         CASE WHEN regexp_like(c.body, '^.{30,170}?[.!?][ ]')
              THEN regexp_replace(c.body, '^(.{30,170}?[.!?])[ ].*$', '$1')
              ELSE c.body END AS body
  FROM clean c
), joined AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN s.head = '' THEN s.body
              WHEN s.body = '' THEN s.head
              ELSE s.head || ' — ' || s.body END AS line
  FROM shortened s
), kept AS (
  SELECT j.line
  FROM joined j
  WHERE LENGTH(j.line) >= 15
    -- A short line ending in a colon is a section label, not a finding.
    AND NOT (LENGTH(j.line) < 40 AND j.line LIKE '%:')
    -- The agent narrates before it reports, and that narration lands glued to the report header.
    -- Listed openers rather than a clever rule, so the next one is one string away.
    AND NOT regexp_like(j.line, '^(Analyzing |Good, enough data|Let me |I dug |Info: )')
), numbered AS (
  SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER () AS seq,
         CASE WHEN LENGTH(k.line) > 200 THEN SUBSTR(k.line, 1, 197) || '...' ELSE k.line END AS insight
  FROM kept k
), ranked AS (
  -- Number before deduplicating, not after: SELECT DISTINCT hashes the rows and the findings come
  -- back in hash order, which for advice is nonsense -- the report puts its most important one first.
  -- MIN(seq) keeps a repeated line where it first appeared; an empty standup says "Nothing to
  -- report." once per section and needs to say it once here.
  SELECT MIN(n.seq) AS seq, n.insight AS insight
  FROM numbered n
  GROUP BY n.insight
), meta AS (
  -- The capture time, on the panel rather than in its description. This is a stored
  -- document and not a query result: the newest capture in range, which the time picker
  -- does not change. Said where it is read, because a tooltip is not where anyone looks
  -- before trusting a number. No captures in range means no row, so the panel stays empty
  -- rather than announcing a NULL date.
  SELECT to_char(to_timestamp_micros(MAX(a._timestamp)), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS captured
  FROM copilot_chronicle_advice a
  WHERE a.service_user IN (${developer})
                AND a.service_user <> 'schema_seed'
                AND to_timestamp_micros(a._timestamp) >= to_timestamp('2026-07-09T00:00:00Z')
                AND a.chronicle_command = 'tips'
)
SELECT h.insight AS "insight"
FROM (
  SELECT 0 AS seq,
         'Captured ' || m.captured || ' UTC - latest capture only, not filtered by the time picker' AS insight
  FROM meta m
  WHERE m.captured IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT r.seq, CAST(r.seq AS VARCHAR) || '. ' || r.insight
  FROM ranked r
) h
ORDER BY h.seq
